![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114537/assets/d7db51d6af763e8853f815feb6e74b88d0ca9a19e79c42b3a42da4e8b088f93c.png)

Consider the region $D$ shown above. If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}x+y, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}(x+y)\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-2,2]\times [-1,1]$
- $R=[0,2]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}x+y, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}(x+y)\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given rectangles.

- Rectangles I and II do not cover the region $D.$

- Rectangle III covers the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
